question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡({sin}^{2}⁡x)] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot [-\frac{1}{|{sin}^{2}⁡x|\sqrt{1+{({sin}^{2}⁡x)}^{2}}}]\cdot {({sin}^{2}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{sin}^{2}⁡x\sqrt{1+{sin}^{4}⁡x}}\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{sin}^{4}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{\sqrt{1+{sin}^{4}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}
$$
